about: Hide the Pain Harold is a stock photo of a white-haired, white-bearded older man in a checked shirt, sitting at a glass desk with a laptop and holding up a pale pink mug. He is smiling broadly for the camera, but his eyes look strained and tired, as if the smile is the only thing holding him together. The gap between that cheerful office-stock-photo pose and the obvious discomfort in his face is the entire joke. He is the patron saint of pretending things are fine: smiling through bad news, awkward moments and situations where showing your real feelings is not an option.
origin: The photos are stock images of Hungarian retired engineer András Arató, who modeled for a photographer and ended up in a series of everyday stock shots. Forum users started noticing his pained smile around 2011, nicknamed him Harold, and he later spoke publicly about accepting his role as a meme.
usage:
The top box sets up a moment of pain or awkwardness, usually "when" plus a situation you cannot complain about. The bottom box completes it with the detail that makes it hurt, or with what Harold says while smiling through it.

It is strongest when the pain is socially hidden: a boss reading your screen, a gift you dislike, a group project, back pain at a family photo shoot. Keep the tone bittersweet rather than dark.
